title: Runbook exercise observations and playbook refresh
content:
Purpose:
This document captures notes and actionable items from the SRE runbook table-top exercise conducted 2026-10-14. The goal was to validate operational playbooks against two realistic incident scenarios, identify gaps in alerts/runbooks, and propose targeted changes to reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) while protecting our latency SLOs.

Exercise summary:
- Facilitators: Aisha Patel (SRE), Liam Chen (serving-runtime eng)
- Participants: 6 (primary on-call, secondary on-call, serving runtime SME, observability engineer, product PM, incident commander trainee)
- Duration: 90 minutes (40m scenario 1, 35m scenario 2, 15m debrief)
- Scenarios exercised: 
  1) Cache invalidation regression: a deploy causes missing KV-prefix hits -> 2x p50/p95 increases across hosted-api region-us-west, partial degradation but error rate stable.
  2) Burst cold-starts: autoscaler misconfiguration + model variant mismatch causes queue growth and retry storms during a model rollout.

Timeline & key decisions (scenario 1):
- 00:00-05:00: Alert fires: latency-p95-up for /v1/generate in us-west. Pager routed to primary on-call (SRE-A).
- 05:00-12:00: Initial triage: logs show cache-miss ratio spike + KV-store request latency increased; serving-runtime SME suggests examine recent rollout and caching flags.
- 12:00-22:00: Scoped mitigation: shift traffic to variant-v2 (fallback) using routing policy; implement short-term autoscaler increase to prevent queueing.
- 22:00-30:00: Root cause hypothesis confirmed: new deploy changed a cache key namespace. Rollback of the deploy avoided further regression; post-action: update rollout checklist to include cache namespace verification.

Timeline & key decisions (scenario 2):
- 00:00-06:00: Alert: request queue depth and retry-count spikes, error-rate creeping upward (0.6% -> 1.8%).
- 06:00-18:00: Triage identifies traffic shift to a quantized model build lacking a warmed KV cache and with higher cold-start overhead.
- 18:00-28:00: Immediate mitigation: scale reserve nodes and enable aggressive pre-warming for rollout; throttle canary ratio to 5% while validating.
- 28:00-40:00: Observability gap: dashboards did not include per-variant cold-start metrics; added as critical action item.

What went well:
- Playbook decision points were clear: team executed fallback routing and rollback steps quickly in simulation.
- Communication template (IC -> exec updates) worked; stakeholders got concise status updates.
- Runbook branching for traffic steering proved useful and was exercised without confusion.

Gaps & risks uncovered:
1) Ambiguous runbook steps around cache namespace checks: multiple teams have different conventions for cache keys (serving-runtime vs model-onboarding). Risk: silent regressions during model deploys.
2) Alerts are noisy for intermediate latency deviations (p95 up by 10-20%) and are not correlated with cache-miss signals. This leads to paging for transient blips.
3) Lack of per-variant cold-start observability. When model variants are rolled, we lack clear metrics to separate cold-start latency vs steady-state latency.
4) On-call compounding load: during burst scenarios, secondary on-call is not automatically paged until a threshold is crossed; threshold too high for steady degradation.

Proposed runbook/playbook updates (short-term):
- Add a "cache-namespace checklist" to the model rollout section: explicit step to assert keyprefix conventions, include a predeploy smoke test that checks prefix hits. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-10-21.
- Implement composite alert rule: latency-p95 + cache-miss-rate correlation to reduce false-positive pages. Owner: Soraya Ahmed. Due: 2026-10-28.
- Add per-variant cold-start metrics to hosted-api dashboards (cold-start count, first-token latency per-variant). Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2026-11-04.
- Adjust paging policy: introduce soft escalation to secondary on-call at sustained p95 > 1.25x baseline for 10 minutes (instead of current 20). Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-10-20.

Longer-term engineering workstreams:
- Automated runbook smoke harness: small CI job that runs preflight checks for model rollouts (prefix checks, small inference to warm cache). Preferred to live in runbooks repo as a GitHub Actions workflow. Linked PR skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/87.
- Improve alert taxonomy and hop-by-hop tracing across routing layers so we can automatically map an alert to likely root-cause subsystems (cache vs kernel vs autoscaler).

On-call handoff template (recommended update):
- Current state: list all active incidents with a one-line status, on-call owner, any mitigation in place, outstanding action items.
- Recommended additions: last successful smoke-test id, recent deploy hash that touched cache code, per-variant warming status, expected maintenance windows.
- Example line: "INC-4821: partial p95 regression (us-west) — rollback applied, traffic steered to variant-v2, follow-up: add cache prefix smoke-test (owner Diego)"

Action items (consolidated):
- Diego: add cache-namespace checklist + implement smoke test (due 2026-10-21).
- Soraya: implement composite alert rule and reduce noise (due 2026-10-28).
- Liam: dashboard tile for per-variant cold-start metrics + instrumentation PR (due 2026-11-04).
- Aisha: update on-call escalation thresholds + publish new handoff template (due 2026-10-20).
- Team: schedule follow-up "runbook validation" session to exercise updated checklist (tentative 2026-11-02).

Next steps & meeting cadence:
- Owners to file targeted tickets and link back to this doc by 2026-10-16.
- Quick sync (30m) to review PRs and dashboards on 2026-10-22.
- Next table-top: include a multi-region failover scenario (Q4 exercise).

Notes & references:
- Exercise recording: internal Zoom (link posted in shared channel).
- Related tickets: JIRA-INC-4821 (simulated), JIRA-OPS-397 (alert noise rewrite RFC).
- Follow-up PR (runbook CI): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/87

Appendix: quick checklist draft to be inserted into runbook:
- Confirm cache keyprefixes used by model artifacts (list prefixes).
- Run local smoke test hitting /v1/generate for canary traffic.
- Verify per-variant warm_count > 50 before increasing canary ratio.
- If p95 > baseline*1.25 for >10m escalate to secondary on-call.

End of notes.
summary: Table-top runbook exercise notes: two simulated incidents (cache namespace regression and cold-start burst), identified runbook ambiguity, alert noise, and missing per-variant observability. Action items assigned with due dates.
